arxiv-2111-13539.title: GeoNeRF: Generalizing NeRF with Geometry Priors
arxiv-2111-13539.creator: Mohammad Mahdi Johari, Yann Lepoittevin, François Fleuret
arxiv-2111-13539.description: Abstract We present GeoNeRF, a generalizable photorealistic novel view synthesis method based on neural radiance fields. Our approach consists of two main stages: a geometry reasoner and a renderer. To render a novel view, the geometry reasoner first constructs cascaded cost volumes for each nearby source view.

arxiv-2201-01684.title: Dynamic GPU Energy Optimization for Machine Learning Training Workloads
arxiv-2201-01684.creator: Farui Wang, Weizhe Zhang, Shichao Lai, Meng Hao, and Zheng Wang
arxiv-2201-01684.description: Abstract GPUs are widely used to accelerate the training of machine learning workloads. As modern machine learning models become increasingly larger, they require a longer time to train, leading to higher GPU energy consumption. This paper presents GPOEO, an online GPU energy optimization framework for machine learning training workloads.

arxiv-2211-11563.title: Quantum chemical computations of gas-phase glycolaldehyde deuteration and constraints to its formation route
arxiv-2211-11563.creator: Fanny Vazart, Cecilia Ceccarelli, Dimitrios Skouteris, Nadia Balucani
arxiv-2211-11563.description: Abstract Despite the detection of numerous interstellar complex organic molecules (iCOMs) for decades, it is still a matter of debate whether they are synthesized in the gas-phase or on the icy surface of interstellar grains. In the past, molecular deuteration has been used to constrain the formation paths of small and abundant hydrogenated interstellar species.

arxiv-2306-01840.title: Spatiotemporal Control of Two-Color Terahertz Generation
arxiv-2306-01840.creator: T. T. Simpson, J. J. Pigeon, M. V. Ambat, K. G. Miller, D. Ramsey, K. Weichman, D. H. Froula, J. P. Palastro
arxiv-2306-01840.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by T. T. Simpson, J. J. Pigeon, M. V. Ambat, K. G. Miller, D. Ramsey, K. Weichman, D. H. Froula, J. P. Palastro. A laser pulse composed of a fundamental and properly phased second harmonic exhibits an asymmetric electric field that can drive a time-dependent current of photoionized electrons. The current produces an ultrashort burst of terahertz (THz) radiation. When driven by a conventional laser pulse, the THz radiation is emitted into a cone with an angle determined by the dispersion of the medium.

arxiv-2312-04448.title: Relativistic materials from an alternative viewpoint
arxiv-2312-04448.creator: Ann E. Mattsson, Daniel A. Rehn
arxiv-2312-04448.description: Abstract Electrons in materials containing heavy elements are fundamentally relativistic and should in principle be described using the Dirac equation. However, the current standard for treatment of electrons in such materials involves density functional theory methods originally formulated from the Schrödinger equation.

arxiv-2408-14960.description: Abstract The use of synthetic data has played a critical role in recent state-of-art breakthroughs. However, overly relying on a single oracle teacher model to generate data has been shown to lead to model collapse and invite propagation of biases.

arxiv-2509-22961.title: A queuing theory-based operating capacity model for multi-modal port operations
arxiv-2509-22961.creator: Debojjal Bagchi, Kyle Bathgate, Stephen D. Boyles, Kenneth N. Mitchell, Magdalena I. Asborno, Marin M. Kress
arxiv-2509-22961.description: Abstract This paper investigates how “operating capacity” can be meaningfully defined in multi-modal maritime freight systems with limited data. Shipping channels and ports are complex systems that interact deeply, and the capacities of individual components may differ from the overall capacity of these systems.

pmc-11536478.description: In patients with out‐of‐hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) who attain return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), rearrest while in the prehospital setting represents a significant barrier to survival. To date, there are limited data to guide prehospital emergency medical services (EMS) management immediately following successful resuscitation resulting in ROSC and prior to handoff in the emergency department.

pmc-11692288.title: ASSOCIATION OF SLEEP MEASURES WITH IMMUNE CELL PHENOTYPES IN THE FRAMINGHAM HEART STUDY
pmc-11692288.creator: Ahmed Ragab, Jiachen Chen, Yumeng Cao, Margaret Doyle, Kathryn Lunetta, Joanne Murabito
pmc-11692288.description: Sleep plays a significant role in regulating immune functions. Disordered sleep is linked to higher risk of infection and chronic inflammation. The relationship between sleep and the immune system is reciprocal, with each influencing the other. Adequate sleep is crucial for maintaining a balanced immune response and overall health.

pmc-12432063.title: Temporal trends in acute care costs of hip fracture treatment from 2011 to 2021 in Japan
pmc-12432063.creator: Masaki Hatano, Hideo Yasunaga, Hisatoshi Ishikura, Takeyuki Tanaka, Shotaro Aso, Sakae Tanaka
pmc-12432063.description: SummaryWe investigated annual trends in acute care costs for hip fracture treatment in Japan from 2011 to 2021. While gross medical costs and costs per hospitalization initially declined, both increased after 2013 and 2014, respectively. In contrast, daily medical costs per person rose steadily throughout the study period.

pmc-12599694.description: Introduction:Chemical burns occur when the human body is exposed to certain chemicals, causing immediate injury, continued invasion, or absorption, leading to progressive local damage or systemic poisoning. Despite the obvious presence of easily accessible toxic products in daily life, the incidence of chemical burns in children is increasing.

pmc-12721750.title: Microsurgical Intervention for Dens Invaginatus in an Immature Tooth: A Case Report With Long‐Term Follow‐Up
pmc-12721750.creator: Talal Al-Nahlawi, Zohreh Moradipour, Hadi Assadian
pmc-12721750.description: Dens invaginatus (DI) is a rare dental anomaly characterized by the infolding of enamel and dentin into the pulp cavity during tooth development. This condition often leads to complex endodontic challenges, predisposing affected teeth to caries, pulp necrosis, and chronic periapical abscesses.

pmc-13183766.title: Single-cell profiling and machine learning identify cuproptosis-related fibroblast subpopulations and fibrogenesis modulator AEBP1 in endometriosis
pmc-13183766.creator: Erqing Huang, Jiang-Tian Li, Danhui Zuo, Ruijie Li, Qingyue Wu, Na Lin, Jinru Zhao, Huajing Wang, Yi Liu, Ling Zhang
pmc-13183766.description: Endometriosis is characterized by progressive fibrosis and limited therapeutic options. Cuproptosis, a copper-dependent form of regulated cell death, has been implicated in multiple pathological conditions, but its relevance to fibroblast-mediated fibrotic progression in endometriosis remains unclear. Single-cell RNA sequencing data from normal, eutopic, and ectopic endometrial tissues were analyzed to assess cuproptosis-related gene (CRG) activity and fibroblast heterogeneity.

Several studies have identified molecular alterations associated with lesion histology and progression.

pmc-13383261.title: A Nonbenzenoid Nanographene Horse Saddle With Four Pentagon–Octagon Pairs
pmc-13383261.creator: Qiang Huang, Yubin Fu, Zongbao Zhang, Jinjin Ding, Mengyuan Yu, Xinyang Ge, Boris Borrisov, Hartmut Komber, Zhen‐Lin Qiu, Yana Vaynzof, Ji Ma, Xinliang Feng

Herein, we report an unprecedented horse‐saddle non‐benzenoid NG (HN1) embedding four pairs of pentagon–octagon units.

pmc-13556513.title: 715. Hippocampal cellular and molecular representations of fear memory reconsolidation and extinction
pmc-13556513.creator: S Kida
pmc-13556513.description: BackgroundMemory retrieval is not a passive phenomenon. Previous studies have presented evidence that memory retrieval is a dynamic process during which memories can be made stronger, weakened, or their content can be altered. Recent studies have shown that reactivated memory becomes labile after retrieval and is re-stabilized through a gene expression-dependent process known as memory reconsolidation.

uslaw-usc-t26-s5385.title: 26 U.S.C. § 5385 — Specially sweetened natural wines
uslaw-usc-t26-s5385.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t26-s5385.description: United States Code, Title 26 (Internal Revenue Code); Chapter 51 (Distilled Spirits, Wines, And Beer); Subchapter F (Bonded And Taxpaid Wine Premises); Part III (Cellar Treatment And Classification Of Wine). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Definition Specially sweetened natural wine is the product made by adding to natural wine of the winemaker’s own production a sufficient quantity of pure dry sugar.

uslaw-usc-t44-s2201.title: 44 U.S.C. § 2201 — Definitions
uslaw-usc-t44-s2201.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t44-s2201.description: United States Code, Title 44 (Public Printing And Documents); Chapter 22 (Presidential Records). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. As used in this chapter— (1) The term “documentary material” means all books, correspondence, memoranda, documents, papers, pamphlets, works of art, models, pictures, photographs, plats, maps, films, and motion pictures, including, but not limited to, audio and visual records, or other electronic or mechanical.
